A contract has two sides: the success case and the failure case. `POST` creates
a resource — send a dictionary as JSON with `json=${body}`. And a good API test
also asserts the **error contract**: a missing product should return `404`, not
a surprise.

Use `expected_status=404` so the request keyword treats the 404 as expected
instead of failing.

## Task 1 — POST an order and assert a 404 for a missing product

**Goal:** create `checks/post.robot` with two tests — one that POSTs an order and
asserts a `201`, and one that GETs a missing product and asserts a `404`.

Here is the same success-and-failure pair over different data. Adapt it.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library     RequestsLibrary
Resource    ../resources/api.resource

*** Test Cases ***
Ordering A Backpack Returns 201
    ${body}=    Create Dictionary    product=trail-backpack    quantity=1
    ${resp}=    POST    ${API_URL}/api/orders    json=${body}
    Status Should Be    201    ${resp}
    Should Be Equal    ${resp.json()}[status]    complete

Missing Product Is A 404
    ${resp}=    GET    ${API_URL}/api/products/ghost    expected_status=404
    Should Be Equal    ${resp.json()}[error]    product not found
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** both tests are defined.

<!-- hint -->
Build the order body with `Create Dictionary    product=travel-mug    quantity=2`,
then `POST    ${API_URL}/api/orders    json=${body}` and assert `201`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
For the error test, pass `expected_status=404` on the GET so the keyword accepts
it, then assert `Should Be Equal    ${resp.json()}[error]    product not found`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library     RequestsLibrary
Resource    ../resources/api.resource

*** Test Cases ***
Placing An Order Returns 201
    ${body}=    Create Dictionary    product=travel-mug    quantity=2
    ${resp}=    POST    ${API_URL}/api/orders    json=${body}
    Status Should Be    201    ${resp}
    Should Be Equal    ${resp.json()}[status]    complete

Unknown Product Is A 404
    ${resp}=    GET    ${API_URL}/api/products/nope    expected_status=404
    Should Be Equal    ${resp.json()}[error]    product not found
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run both green

Run:

```bash
uv run robot checks
```

**Check:** the order posts with `201`, and the missing product returns `404`.
